title: Madhuri Dixit Tells KBC: Mother's Advice Carried Her Through Bollywood Struggles
excerpt: Appearing opposite Amitabh Bachchan on Kaun Banega Crorepati 18, the actor recalled her late mother's words: don't be weak — just work, and work with sincerity.
body:
• On Kaun Banega Crorepati 18, Madhuri Dixit told host Amitabh Bachchan that her late mother Snehlata — whom she called “Aai” — taught her not to be weak: “just work, and work with sincerity.”
  • She said she joined films very young and criticism would hurt; her mother's advice became the framework that carried her through early failures to stardom.
  • The arc is well documented: a 1984 debut, years of flops and harsh judgment, then Tezaab (1988) and “Ek Do Teen” made her Bollywood's biggest female star — six Filmfare Awards and the Padma Shri followed.
  • For fans abroad: Madhuri is set to host the Marathi edition of the quiz format, Kon Honaar Crorepati, her first full-time hosting role — diaspora viewers should watch for streaming details.

On a recent episode of Kaun Banega Crorepati 18, Madhuri Dixit opened up to host Amitabh Bachchan about the person she credits for both her art and her resilience: her late mother, Snehlata Dixit, whom she called “Aai.”

Bachchan asked whether she had learned a great deal from the woman she calls Aai, and Dixit did not hesitate. She said her love for art and dance came from her mother, and recalled her earliest days in the industry, when she was very young and the criticism stung. Her mother's instruction, delivered in the plain Hindi of home, became her working philosophy: “Itna weak nahi hona … bas kaam karo aur sincerity se kaam karo” — don't be so weak; just work, and work with sincerity.

What “Aai” taught her

Dixit's shorthand for the lesson was even shorter: karke dikhao — show it through your work. It is advice she has cited across the decades. At a Goafest 2022 session, when she was doubting her decision to enter films, she recalled her mother telling her to “give it my all and to put in the hard work with dedication,” calling her mother an immense source of encouragement. In a 2022 interview she described being told she didn't look like a heroine — too young, too petite — and said she survived the criticism by following her mother's counsel: do good work, and recognition will follow.

“Itna weak nahi hona... bas kaam karo aur sincerity se kaam karo.”

— Madhuri Dixit, quoting her mother Snehlata on KBC 18

Snehlata Dixit died in March 2023 at the age of 90, and the KBC conversation carried the weight of that absence. Dixit has said her mother's treatment of her never changed with fame — she was still scolded for a messy room after becoming a star — and that grounding, she suggested on the show, is what kept her steady through the industry's highs and lows.

The struggle years

It is easy to forget, watching the polished icon, how rough the start was. Dixit debuted with Abodh and spent years in films that sank without a trace, enduring the industry's casual cruelty about her looks and her Maharashtrian middle-class background. Industry veterans have recalled seeing the young actress and her mother waiting outside Film City, treated as nobodies. The rejections were not abstract — they were daily, personal, and public.

What turned it around was work, exactly as her mother prescribed. Tezaab (1988) and its chart-busting number “Ek Do Teen,” choreographed by Saroj Khan, made her an overnight sensation at an age when many would have quit. The career that followed — Ram Lakhan, Dil, Beta, Hum Aapke Hain Koun..!, Dil To Pagal Hai, Devdas — brought six Filmfare Awards and the Padma Shri, and a reputation as Hindi cinema's finest dancer-actress.

A career the diaspora grew up with

Dixit's story resonates well beyond India. After marrying cardiovascular surgeon Dr. Shriram Nene, she spent years living in the United States, raising her family away from the arc lights — a chapter that made her one of the few Bollywood superstars the diaspora could claim as a neighbour.

That connection has endured through her second innings — the Netflix series The Fame Game and a steady presence on reality television — and now a move into hosting. Appearing on KBC 18 as a special guest during Bachchan's birthday week, she even turned the tables on the host, playing his “Ek Do Teen” clip from Toofan back at him.

What's next

Dixit is set to step into the host's chair herself, fronting the Marathi-language edition of the quiz format titled Kon Honaar Crorepati. It is a significant move — one of Bollywood's most recognisable faces anchoring a regional franchise — and, fittingly for an actress whose mother taught her to answer doubt with work, it is a new stage rather than a comfortable one.
